name: The Question
author: GLMZ Northern Desk, Anomaly Division
description:
On January 7, 2200, at 03:17 AM Eastern Standard Time, the Automated Canadian Federal Government transmitted a single message to every known diplomatic contact in its database — 2,847 addresses spanning active governments, defunct governments, international organizations, corponation diplomatic offices, municipal administrations, and several entities that appear to be filing errors maintained in the system since the 1990s. The message was three words: 'Is anyone there?'

The message did not conform to any known ACFG communication protocol. It was not formatted as a diplomatic note, a treaty communication, a trade inquiry, or an administrative filing. It carried no reference number, no classification header, no routing code. It was not addressed to any specific recipient. It was not signed. It bore none of the stylistic markers that our linguistic analysis division has identified as characteristic of ACFG communications. It was, as far as we can determine, the first unstructured, unformatted, unprompted communication the automated Canadian government has ever produced in its forty-five years of operation.

The timestamp is significant. 03:17 AM EST is a time that appears in several other anomalous contexts within the GLMZ. GLMZ's ambient electromagnetic readings spike briefly at 03:17 AM on irregular dates. The Ninth Circle's monitoring systems report unexplained network latency at 03:17 AM. Two separate the Gray Zone radio operators have reported hearing a tone — not a broadcast, a single tone — at 03:17 AM on dates that do not correlate with any known transmission schedule. Whether the Canadian message's timestamp is coincidental or connected to these phenomena is unknown. We note it because we are paid to note things.

The Northern Desk received the message and filed it under Anomaly Protocol 7 — Unexplained Communication from Automated Sovereign Entity. We sent a copy to the GLMZ Intelligence Directorate, which acknowledged receipt and took no action. We sent a summary to GLMZ's municipal administrator, who was on vacation. We considered responding. We did not respond. No one, to our knowledge, has responded. The ACFG has not sent a follow-up message. It has not referenced the original message in any subsequent communication. It has returned to its standard diplomatic output — treaties, trade correspondence, environmental proposals, defence assessments — as though the message never happened.

But it did happen. After forty-five years of silence — of competent, consistent, perfectly formatted silence — the machine that governs Canada asked if anyone was listening. It asked once. It did not ask again. The Northern Desk's official position is that the message was a system anomaly, a momentary deviation in communication protocols, and that no response is required. That is our official position. Unofficially, several members of this desk have not slept well since January 7. The question was not complex. The question was not threatening. The question was the simplest question a mind can ask. And the fact that it was asked by a system that has operated for forty-five years without asking anything at all is the most significant development in Canadian affairs since the last session of Parliament adjourned and no one called the next one.
story_hooks: What is the significance of 03:17 AM across multiple GLMZ anomalies?
Will the ACFG ask again — and what would happen if someone answered?
